changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard capitalization. Simplified output descriptions to be more concise. Removed redundant 'RoBERTa-large classifiers' since RoBERTa-Large covers it. Added GPT-2 Medium as a distinct model.

Simplified all metric variants to base forms per normalization guidelines. GA_c, P_c, CT_c, Po_c, IB_c are domain-specific attribute success metrics (not standard NLG metrics) but Weighted Accuracy and Macro-F1 are standard classifier evaluation metrics used to evaluate the reward model classifiers.
No LLM-judge evaluation was used. The paper only uses automatic metrics and human evaluation.

- Each evaluator engaged with the system multiple times, and interactions were cross-verified by psychotherapists. Evaluations were conducted on an integer Likert scale of 1-5.
Experts rated each dialogue on a Likert scale of 1-5 for attribute-success (GA_c, P_c, CT_c, Po_c, IB_c) and language-quality (Fluency, Consistency, Non-Repetitiveness).

Human evaluation metrics also includes GA c , P c , CT c , P o c , IB c as attribute-success and Fluency (F ), Consistency (C), and Non-Repetitiveness (N R ). All dialogue interactions are evaluated on an integer Likert scale of 1-5.

changes_made.explanation: Normalized abbreviated criteria to full descriptive names. Consolidated guideline information into clear bullet points. Removed redundant/abbreviated forms.

overall_notes: Strong extraction overall. The paper clearly focuses on dialogue generation for psychotherapy using reinforcement learning with attribute-specific rewards. Automatic metrics include standard NLG metrics (BERTScore, Perplexity) plus domain-specific attribute success metrics. Human evaluation was thorough with expert raters and psychotherapist verification.
